title: Partition-aware package staging and operator canary contract
creator: Priya Shah
description: Problem statement: Customers running Redwood Private in strongly isolated networks struggle with multi-stage upgrades where long-lived network partitions or constrained admin windows cause package distribution to fail or leave clusters in partially-upgraded states. This PRD defines a deterministic, operator-driven package staging and canary contract that tolerates transient partitions, bounds egress approvals, and provides clear acceptance criteria for telemetry buffering and artifact chain verification. The goal is to reduce manual operator interventions during controlled upgrades and to provide predictable rollback points when staging detects data-plane regressions.
goals: Define a deterministic package staging protocol that supports split networks and intermittent outbound access windows
Introduce an operator-centric canary window mechanism with explicit success/failure gating and observable failure modes
Provide bounded, auditable egress approval flow (human-in-loop) for customers that require minimal external contact
Ensure telemetry collection is robust for air-gapped installs via local buffering and resumable upload during allowed windows
Create testable acceptance criteria that engineering and SRE can use during canary and rollout phases
non_goals: Re-architecting the entire private bootstrap process (out of scope for this ticket)
Building new proprietary artifact distribution network (we rely on customer mirrors/relays)
Replacing existing KMS integrations; we will define rotation compatibility only
requirements: Operator-driven staged bundles: ability for operator to prepare an ordered "bundle" of artifacts that include manifests, images, and checksum signatures and mark them as staged for site consumption
Partition-awareness: site agent must apply staged bundles locally when connectivity absent and report state transitions with timestamps
Canary window semantics: operator may declare a canary window (duration, success thresholds, rollback TTL) before promoting bundles to remainder of nodes
Bounded egress approval: approval tokens issued by the control plane can be time-limited, scope-limited (only allow download of listed artifacts) and revocable
Resumable telemetry: local metric/log buffer with size and retention policy; telemetry uploader resumes and reconciles after outbound permissions are granted
Artifact signature chain: every staged bundle must include a signed provenance file and support offline verification using customer KMS or provided public keys
Explicit failure modes: staged bundle application must surface 'partial-apply', 'conflict', and 'verify-failed' states with remediation hints
Operator audit trail: every operator action (stage, approve, revoke, promote, rollback) must be recorded in the site operator log and exposed to the control plane once connectivity resumes
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: A site with a simulated partition (no outbound access) successfully accepts a staged bundle into local agent storage and reports 'staged' in the operator UI within 30 seconds of staging command

AC-2: During a canary window (configurable 15m to 2h), if 80% of canary nodes report 'healthy' after post-install smoke checks, the bundle may be promoted automatically; failure to meet threshold triggers an automatic rollback signal and records failure reason

AC-3: Approval tokens can be issued with a TTL as low as 5 minutes and are honored by site agents; revoked tokens deny new downloads within 10 seconds of revocation and agents stop download attempts within next scheduling tick

AC-4: Telemetry buffer guarantees no more than 10MiB local retention by default and will resume upload and reconcile metrics within 10 minutes of outbound permission restoration; reconciled telemetry must include upload timestamps and sequence numbers
AC-5: Artifact provenance verification must catch modified artifacts: test injects a corrupted artifact and site agent must surface 'verify-failed' and refuse promote/activate paths

AC-6: Operator audit trail entries for stage, approve, promote, revoke, and rollback are synchronized to the control plane within 15 minutes of connectivity restoration and include operator identity and artifact bundle hash
AC-7: Upgrade sequences that require multiple dependency install steps must support idempotent retry; test verifies repeated application does not leave cluster in non-idempotent partial state
AC-8: All behaviors above are covered by an automated integration test that runs in CI and simulates partition, token revocation, and corrupted artifact scenarios
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary lab): implement agent-side staged bundle API, local storage, and verification checks. Run internal lab tests with simulated partitions.
Phase 2 (customer pilot): select 3 customers with VPC-private installs; provide operator training and run controlled canary windows with support staff on call.
Phase 3 (gradual GA): enable bounded egress approval UI in Console, add telemetry buffer controls, and open to all Private customers behind feature flag for two quarters before full rollout
risks: Risk: If operator tokens are mis-issued, a malicious actor could schedule artifact downloads during permitted windows — mitigation: strict RBAC and short TTLs
Risk: Excessive local telemetry buffering can cause disk pressure — mitigation: enforced default retention and configurable limits with alerts
Risk: Complexity for customers with custom air-gap processes — mitigation: documented operator playbooks and optional manual artifact injection path
decisions: We will support both control-plane-issued tokens and an approved-file manifest approach for fully offline customers (manifest path documented but requires manual operator steps)
Default telemetry retention will be conservative (10MiB) with explicit customer override setting
Canary threshold default set to 80% but configurable per site
notes: This contract is intentionally conservative: initial pilot will opt-in customers only. Success is measured by reduction in manual rollback incidents during scheduled upgrades and time-to-full-promotion after staging windows.
follow_up_tasks: Create ENG ticket to implement token revocation websocket (ENG-26459)
Draft operator training slide deck and run two customer onboarding sessions
Add observability signals for local buffer pressure and failed verifications to Console alerts
